# Sea State Explorer

> Free web tool from Thrust Maritime giving long term wave, wind and weather window statistics for any offshore location, from ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF / Copernicus C3S), 2010-2024, 3 hourly. Click a point at sea, pick months, read the percentage of time significant wave height exceeds each threshold.

<!-- generated by tools/build_pages.py, do not edit by hand -->

## What it answers

- How often significant wave height exceeds a given level at a location, by calendar month and across the year
- Mean wave height by month, typical peak period and direction, wind speed (mean and top decile), extreme sea states, counts of calm spells (weather windows), water depth, nearby oil and gas assets, tropical cyclone exposure
- A one page PDF summary and a shareable link for every result

## The data behind it

- ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF / Copernicus C3S), 2010-2024, 3 hourly, 0.5 degree grid. Values are the nearest grid cell to the chosen point, never interpolated; every result states the data point, its distance from the point, the grid and the sample count.
- Attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information [2010-2024]. ERA5 hourly data on single levels (significant height of combined wind waves and swell). Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use of this information.
- These are climatological estimates, not forecasts. They are unreliable close to coastlines and in sheltered or shallow water and may underestimate extremes. Not for design, navigation or operational decisions.

## Citable pages

- [Locations index](https://seastate.thrustm.com/locations/index.html): 85 named offshore working areas, each with a monthly table, the headline numbers in words, the data basis and a citation line
- [Methodology](https://seastate.thrustm.com/methodology.html): how the statistics are computed
- [Explorer](https://seastate.thrustm.com/): any other point at sea; the URL fragment #loc=<lat>,<lon> reproduces a result

## How to cite

- Thrust Maritime, Sea State Explorer, <location>, ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF / Copernicus C3S) 2010-2024, 3 hourly, accessed <date>, <page URL>
- Each location page carries its own ready-made citation line.

## Not for scraping

- The tile files under /data/ are bulk inputs for the interactive map, excluded from crawling in robots.txt, and not a citable surface. Automated bulk extraction is not permitted; the underlying open datasets are available from the original providers credited above.
- The location pages and the methodology page are the reference surface: quote from them and link to them.
